multi_experiment_analysis.notes_tex: Mean and standard deviation of consumption are computed from the long nonlinear simulation and reported as percent log differences from the deterministic steady state. The welfare cost is the consumption-equivalent cost of business cycles, in percent. Capital reallocation is the sum of the absolute sectoral capital-composition changes shown in the stochastic-steady-state figure. Each sectoral change is the percent change in its stochastic-steady-state capital share relative to its deterministic-steady-state share. ``Homogeneous shocks'' sets sectoral shock volatilities to a common value.
